Realm v2.10.0 brings service management, configuration validation, and recovery to `realmctl`. Full and slim Linux packages include both commands, with AMD64 and ARM64 builds for Ubuntu 22.04 and newer and SHA-256 checksums.

## What's new

- Set up or adopt a systemd service with `realmctl setup`, then manage startup, shutdown, boot enablement, logs, and shared settings through the same command.
- Validate enabled rules with `realmctl check`, using Realm's native parser without starting a relay. Applying changes automatically validates the configuration and systemd's effective start command before restarting.
- Verify that the service process owns every expected TCP/UDP listener before reporting a successful start.
- Restore the previous verified configuration after failed startup and retain rejected changes for inspection. Use `realmctl recover` to finish an interrupted apply.
- Resume interrupted imports and recover interrupted service-file updates. Import keeps the source unchanged and does not overwrite or merge existing rules.
- Reject hidden configuration directory names, report directory-loading errors, detect conflicting systemd overrides, and support long service names with bounded backup filenames.

## Install or update

Install **both `realm` and `realmctl` from this release**. The new helper requires the native checker in the matching binary; upgrading the script alone is insufficient.

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phungvanquy/realm/v2.10.0/install.sh | bash -s -- --version v2.10.0
realm --version
realm check --version
```

Add `--slim` for the smaller TCP/UDP build, or `--install-dir "$HOME/.local/bin"` to install without sudo. The installer preserves your configuration and rules.

## Existing installations

Register the service once after upgrading. Choose the command that matches your installation:

| Existing setup | Command |
| --- | --- |
| Service already created by realmctl | `sudo realmctl setup` |
| Manually created service using realmctl's named rules | `sudo realmctl setup --adopt` |
| Service using a single configuration file | `sudo realmctl setup --import /etc/realm/config.toml` |

Import needs a new configuration directory. Keep any custom `--config-dir`, `--service`, and `--binary` selections; see the [migration guide](https://github.com/phungvanquy/realm/blob/v2.10.0/readme.realmctl.md#migrate-an-existing-configuration).

Then validate and apply:

```bash
sudo realmctl check
sudo realmctl apply
realmctl status
```

Applying restarts the service and interrupts existing connections. The first successful `start` or `apply` establishes the verified snapshot used for later rollback. Recovery restores configuration files, not an older binary. Listener checks do not test destination reachability or firewall access.

File changes are saved immediately and can be read by any subsequent service start, including an automatic restart. See [validation and recovery](https://github.com/phungvanquy/realm/blob/v2.10.0/readme.realmctl.md#validation-and-recovery) for recovery commands and limits.
